title: Impleader and potential liability over
summary: Impleader brings a nonparty into an action because that person may owe the defending party all or part of the liability asserted by the plaintiff. Common examples involve indemnity or contribution.
notes: A statement that someone else, rather than the defendant, is directly liable to the plaintiff does not by itself establish the required derivative claim. Rule 14 does not create a substantive right to reimbursement.

sections.Meaning: Impleader brings a nonparty into an action because that person may owe the defending party all or part of the liability asserted by the plaintiff. Common examples involve indemnity or contribution.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the original claim and the substantive source of the proposed third party’s liability to the defendant. Show why that liability depends on or passes through the original claim. Then examine Rule 14’s procedure and the separate jurisdictional requirements.
